hook: Global mangrove forests expanded by 3,200 square miles after 2010.

sections.voiceover: Global mangrove forests expanded by 3,200 square miles after 2010.
sections.visual_cue: Satellite view of green mangrove forest coastal canopy expanding over tidal waters.
b_roll: Landsat satellite aerial imagery of lush coastal mangroves
sections.animation_cue: Slow zoom in on expanding green shoreline

sections.voiceover: Between 1984 and 2010, mangroves shrank from 155,000 square kilometers to 152,000 square kilometers. Where did the 3,200 square miles start?
sections.visual_cue: Coastal map showing historical mangrove decline across global coastlines.
b_roll: Historical map outline of coastal wetland area
sections.animation_cue: Red shaded loss region transitioning to a question icon

sections.voiceover: But NASA Earth Observatory's Landsat imagery showed a rebound across Asia, Australia, and South America.
sections.visual_cue: High-resolution NASA Earth Observatory satellite imagery highlighting fresh mangrove growth.
b_roll: NASA Earth Observatory digital satellite rendering of coastline
sections.animation_cue: Split-screen comparison showing shift in forest density

sections.voiceover: Yale E360 reported growth spanning from Louisiana to Myanmar and West Africa. Landsat data tracked 3,200 square miles of recovery by 2023.
sections.visual_cue: World map illustrating expanding mangrove sites across Louisiana, Myanmar, and West Africa.
b_roll: Mangrove roots submerged in clear coastal water
sections.animation_cue: Animated markers pulsing across global coastlines

sections.voiceover: Global mangrove coverage reversed decades of decline after 2010.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic aerial sweep over dense green mangrove trees meeting the ocean.
b_roll: Overhead camera movement across thriving coastal mangrove canopy
sections.animation_cue: Slow outward pan to wide expanse
